summary:
Devendra Chaplot from Mistral AI presents the company's approach to building and releasing open-source large language models. Founded in June 2023, Mistral AI has released several models: Mistral 7B (September 2023), the first 7B model to achieve 60 on MMLU; Mixtral 8x7B (December 2023), a sparse mixture-of-experts model that uses only a subset of parameters per token for inference efficiency; Mistral Large (February 2024), their flagship with best-in-class reasoning and math; Mixtral 8x22B (April 2024), a larger multilingual MoE supporting English, French, Italian, German, Spanish; and Codestral 22B (June 2024), a code-specific dense Transformer.

Mistral's mission is to bring frontier AI to everyone, focusing on developers. Their principles include openness, portability across Azure, AWS, GCP, VPC, and on-prem, performance-to-speed ratio optimization, and customizability via tools like Mistral fine-tune and Mistral inference libraries.

Chaplot counters the misconception that open source conflicts with profit, arguing they are complementary. Open source serves as branding and marketing (Mistral has no in-house marketing team), aids customer acquisition as users try open models then upgrade to proprietary ones, and benefits from community customization efforts.

He outlines three LLM training stages. Pre-training uses next-token prediction on tens of trillions of tokens, costs tens to hundreds of millions of dollars, and offers limited retraining chances; hyperparameter selection remains partly intuitive. Instruction tuning uses prompt-response pairs with masked prompts, requiring far less compute (~100 GPUs for hours or days). Learning from human feedback uses preference data via RLHF and DPO, since preferences are cheaper to obtain than full annotations.

Codestral 22B is highlighted as a code-specific model fluent in 80+ programming languages, supporting both instruct and fill-in-the-middle modes. It outperforms Code Llama 70B, DeepSeek Coder 33B, and Llama 3 70B while being significantly smaller, with a longer context window than other open-source code models. It is free on chat.mist.ai, available via La Plateforme API, and integrated with VS Code and JetBrains plugins.

Chaplot closes with practical guidance: commercial models are easier for prototyping since they generally don't allow fine-tuning, while open models enable task-specific fine-tuning for better performance-to-cost ratio in production. The recommended workflow is to prototype with the highest-end commercial models, then fine-tune an open-source model like Mistral 7B or Mixtral 8x7B for the specific task. He notes Mistral has offices in Paris and London and is actively hiring.

sections.title: Introduction & Mistral AI Timeline
sections.summary: Chaplot introduces Mistral AI, founded in June 2023, and traces the release timeline: Mistral 7B (Sep 2023), Mixtral 8x7B and platform APIs (Dec 2023), Mistral Large (Feb 2024), Mixtral 8x22B (Apr 2024), and Codestral 22B (Jun 2024).

sections.title: Mission & Principles
sections.summary: Mistral's mission is to bring frontier AI to everyone, focusing on developers. Principles include openness, portability across cloud and on-prem, performance-to-speed ratio optimization, and customizability via fine-tuning libraries and APIs.

sections.title: Open Source Models Overview
sections.summary: Describes three open-sourced models: Mistral 7B (first 7B to reach 60 MMLU, deployable on laptops/phones), Mixtral 8x7B (sparse MoE, uses subset of parameters per token for inference efficiency), and Mixtral 8x22B (larger, multilingual, longer context).

sections.title: Why Open Source
sections.summary: Addresses the misconception that open source conflicts with profit. Open source serves as branding/marketing (no in-house marketing team), customer acquisition funnel to proprietary models, and benefits from community customization and deployment efforts.

sections.title: LLM Training Stages
sections.summary: Covers pre-training (next-token prediction on tens of trillions of tokens, costing tens to hundreds of millions of dollars, hyperparameter selection partly intuitive), instruction tuning (prompt-response pairs with masked prompts, ~100 GPUs for hours/days), and learning from human feedback (RLHF and DPO using preference data).

sections.title: Codestral 22B
sections.summary: Codestral 22B is a dense Transformer for code, fluent in 80+ programming languages, supporting instruct and fill-in-the-middle modes. It outperforms Code Llama 70B, DeepSeek Coder 33B, and Llama 3 70B while being significantly smaller, with a longer context window.

sections.title: Practical Tips & Closing
sections.summary: Codestral is free on chat.mist.ai and La Plateforme API (free until end of July), with VS Code and JetBrains plugin integration. Chaplot gives practical guidance: prototype with commercial models using prompt engineering, few-shot, Chain of Thought, and RAG, then fine-tune open-source models like Mistral 7B or Mixtral 8x7B for production to optimize performance-to-cost. He notes Mistral has offices in Paris and London and is hiring researchers, engineers, and business/marketing staff. No Q&A is taken.

limitations: Pre-training hyperparameter selection is not exact science and relies on intuition and experience
Best hyperparameters for smaller models may not transfer to larger models
Pre-trained models cannot interact with humans as desired without instruction tuning and RLHF
Noisy data in pre-training can hurt model performance—more data does not necessarily mean better performance
Small companies may not get funding for a second training run if the first fails
